briefdescription.para: Deprecated access to the verbosity level.

detaileddescription.para: Kept from the v5.0.1 reporter class, for the applications that read it through the deprecated runner::reporter() (tr.reporter ().verbosity ()). The level is the one returned by runner::verbosity_level(), from the same session options.

simplesect.para: The verbosity level of the session.

detaileddescription.para: Returns the level stored in verbosity_, set by the constructor.

briefdescription.para: The position in the buffer where the expression of a failed check begins.

detaileddescription.para: Set by output_fail_prefix(), after the condition: key, and used by output_fail_suffix() to write the expression appended between the two calls as a YAML double-quoted scalar. It is std::string::npos when the failure has no expression.

briefdescription.para: The position in the buffer where the description of a passed check begins.

detaileddescription.para: Set by output_pass_prefix() and used by output_pass_suffix() to escape the description, which is the message, or the expression appended between the two calls when there is no message.

briefdescription.para: Deleted copy constructor to prevent copying.

detaileddescription.para: The reporter owns the output buffer and the output file, which must not be shared.

briefdescription.para: Constructor for the reporter_tap class.

detaileddescription.para:
opts
The session options, passed to runner::initialise() or parsed by it from the command line.
Delegates construction to the reporter base class with the supplied options. If tracing is enabled, the function signature is output for diagnostic purposes.

briefdescription.para: Deleted move constructor to prevent moving.

detaileddescription.para: The reporter is owned by the runner, through a pointer, and is never relocated.

briefdescription.para: Destructor for the reporter_tap class.

detaileddescription.para: The output file, if any, is closed by the base class destructor.
No resources are owned directly by reporter_tap; the destructor performs no explicit clean-up. If tracing is enabled, the function signature is output for diagnostic purposes.

briefdescription.para: Reports the abort of the test execution.

detaileddescription.para: Displays the buffered check results, followed by a Bail out! line with the location of the failed requirement, or of the runner::abort() call.

location
The source location of the failed requirement, or of the runner::abort() call.
is_requirement
true if the abort is caused by a failed requirement.
Returns
Nothing.
Since end_test_case() is not called for the running test cases, this member function writes the buffered lines, if any, in its place (after a failed requirement, they end with it), preceded, with normal or verbose verbosity, by the headings of the open test cases, if not displayed yet, followed by an unindented Bail out! <reason> at <file>:<line> line, with the file name escaped as the reason, which tells the TAP consumers that the run stopped early (see the TAP 14 specification), not that the output was truncated. The reason is Requirement failed after a failed requirement, and Test execution aborted for an explicit call of runner::abort().

Both are always written to the output file, as in end_test_case(), and, unless the verbosity is silent, to stdout, preceded by an empty line when add_empty_line_ is set. With quiet verbosity, which otherwise displays only the summary, the failed checks are displayed as comments, and the Bail out! line as well, since the summary is never reached.
The buffer is then cleared, so that its lines are not written again, should the abort handler throw an exception that the application catches.

briefdescription.para: Marks the beginning of a test session.

detaileddescription.para:
runner
Reference to the test runner.
Returns
Nothing.
If verbosity is not silent, emits a blank line to stdout and then calls write_info() to output build and environment information. The TAP version header "TAP version 14" is then written to the output file (if open) and, unless verbosity is silent, to stdout. The add_empty_line_ flag is cleared so that the first suite header is not separated by an extra blank line.

briefdescription.para: Marks the beginning of a test suite.

detaileddescription.para:
suite
Reference to the test suite.
Returns
Nothing.
Emits a "# Subtest: <name>" comment line to mark the start of a TAP test case block for the suite; the line breaks in the name are replaced by spaces (see tap_text()). The line is written to the output file when one is open. Under normal or verbose verbosity, it is also written to stdout, preceded by a blank line when add_empty_line_ is set.

briefdescription.para: Marks the beginning of a test case.

detaileddescription.para:
test_case
Reference to the test case.
Returns
Nothing.
For a nested test case, the results of the checks already performed by the outer test case, if any, are written first (see commit_outer_results()), so that the output follows the execution order.

A "# Subtest: <name>" comment line (indented according to nesting depth), with the line breaks in the name replaced by spaces, is then written to the output file and, under verbose verbosity, to stdout as well. With the other verbosity levels, the heading is displayed later, only if something is displayed under it (see display_open_headers()).

briefdescription.para: Returns the TAP comment prefix string "# ".

detaileddescription.para:
Parameters
None.
The string "# ", used to prefix comment lines in TAP output.
Returns "# ". The TAP reporter prefixes all comment lines, including the informational lines emitted by write_info(), with the TAP comment marker.

briefdescription.para: Appends a line ending to the internal output buffer.

detaileddescription.para: Nothing is written to the console or to the output file; the buffer is written by the concrete reporters, at the end of each test case or suite.

Parameters
None.
Returns
Nothing.
This member function appends a newline character to the internal output buffer of the reporter. The buffer itself is written later, by the concrete reporters, at the end of each test case or suite, which then also flush the streams.

briefdescription.para: Marks the end of a test session.

detaileddescription.para:
runner
Reference to the test runner.
Returns
Nothing.
Emits the TAP plan line (1..N, where N is the total number of test suites) followed by a comment line summarising passed checks, failed checks, executed test cases, suite count, and elapsed time. The numbers of test cases and of suites skipped by the filter follow the respective counts, only when not zero. Both lines are written to the output file when one is open, and, unless verbosity is silent, to stdout. With quiet verbosity, the plan matches the ok/not ok lines of the suites displayed by end_suite() and skip_suite(), so that the console output is a complete TAP document, which node-tap and the other TAP consumers read as failed when a suite failed; no empty line precedes it.

briefdescription.para: Marks the end of a test suite.

detaileddescription.para:
suite
Reference to the test suite.
Returns
Nothing.
Emits the TAP plan line for the suite's test cases, and for the failure of the suite body, if any (see fail_suite()), followed by an ok/not ok result line that includes the suite index, name, pass/fail status, check counts, test case count, and elapsed time; the name is escaped (see tap_text()). Any output accumulated in buffer_ is written to the output file and, with normal or verbose verbosity, when verbosity is verbose or the suite failed, to stdout as well; the plan and result lines are written to stdout with normal or verbose verbosity. With quiet verbosity, only the result line is written to stdout, without the plan and without an empty line, so that the session plan written by end_session() counts the displayed lines; the failure of the suite body, if any, precedes it, as comments (see write_quiet_failures()). The buffer is cleared on exit.

briefdescription.para: Marks the end of a test case.

detaileddescription.para:
test_case
Reference to the test case.
Returns
Nothing.
Emits the TAP plan line for the test case's checks and nested test cases, followed by an ok/not ok result line that includes the test case index, escaped name, pass/fail status, and check counts. As in node-tap, the result is not ok when a check or a nested test case failed; the number of failed nested test cases is added when it is not zero. Any output accumulated in buffer_ and the two lines are always written to the output file.

With normal verbosity, a passed test case that has nothing displayed under it (no nested test case, and no committed checks) is displayed as a single test point, the ok line, without the # Subtest: heading, the plan, and the checks; this is a valid test point, and it keeps the console output short. Otherwise, with normal or verbose verbosity, the test case is displayed as a complete block, with the headings of the outer test cases first, if not displayed yet, all the buffered checks, the plan, and the result line, so that the plan matches the displayed test points, with the test point numbers unchanged. With quiet verbosity, only the failed checks are displayed, as comments (see write_quiet_failures()).
The buffer is cleared on exit.

briefdescription.para: Reports a failed condition.

detaileddescription.para:
failure
The failure details: the kind of the check, the message to display, whether the expression text is displayed, and the source location of the failure.
expression
The string representation of the expression.
test_case
The test case that owns this check.
Returns
Nothing.
Outputs a fail prefix (which includes the message and the source location), followed, when failure.has_expression is true, by the pre-formatted expression string, and a fail suffix.

briefdescription.para: Reports a failure of a test suite outside its test cases.

detaileddescription.para: Adds a not ok <n> - <message> test point, at the indentation of the test cases, to the output buffer, which end_suite() displays.

message
The message to display.
suite
Reference to the test suite.
Returns
Nothing.
Adds a not ok <n> - <message> line, with the message escaped (see tap_text()), to the output buffer, indented as the test cases of the suite, where <n> is the current test point number of the suite, which follows the test cases already run, and is therefore counted in the plan of the suite. Since there is no source location, no YAML diagnostics block follows. The line is displayed by end_suite(), with the other buffered output of the failed suite.

briefdescription.para: Flushes the standard output stream and the output file.

detaileddescription.para: Only the C streams are flushed; the internal output buffer is not written.

Parameters
None.
Returns
Nothing.
This member function flushes the stdout stream and, if open, the output file, so that everything already written to them becomes visible. It does not write the contents of the internal buffer.

briefdescription.para: Returns whether the output file could not be opened.

detaileddescription.para: Checked by runner::initialise(), which reports it as an option error; the report is then written only to the console.

Parameters
None.
true
The output file was requested but could not be opened.
false
No output file was requested, or it was opened.
Returns the flag set by the constructor when fopen() failed.

briefdescription.para: Output operator for boolean values.

detaileddescription.para:
v
The boolean value to output.
Reference to the current reporter instance.
This operator overload appends "true" or "false" to the internal output buffer of the reporter, as the expression formatter does. Being a non-template function, it is selected for bool values instead of the arithmetic template, which would format them as numbers.

briefdescription.para: Output operator for a single character.

detaileddescription.para:
c
The character to output.
Reference to the current reporter instance.
This operator overload appends the specified character to the internal output buffer of the reporter.

briefdescription.para: Output operator for a constant character string.

detaileddescription.para: Also selected for the non-const char pointers and arrays, which the pointer template does not accept. A null pointer is output as "nullptr".

s
The string to output, or a null pointer.
Reference to the current reporter instance.
This operator overload appends the contents of the provided C-style string to the internal output buffer of the reporter, or "nullptr" for a null pointer, as the expression formatter does; the char* values also reach this overload, and std::string::append() must not be called with a null pointer.

briefdescription.para: Output operator for the indentation manipulator.

detaileddescription.para: Appends indent_size_ spaces for each indentation level.

m
The indentation manipulator produced by indent(n).
Reference to the current reporter instance.
This operator overload appends spaces to the internal output buffer, indent_size_ for each of the m.level indentation levels, allowing *this << indent(n) << "text" chaining in both reporters.

briefdescription.para: Output operator for stream manipulators, such as endl.

detaileddescription.para:
func
Function pointer to the stream manipulator.
Reference to the current reporter instance.
This operator overload enables manipulators, such as endl, to be used with the reporter stream in a manner similar to standard C++ streams. When a manipulator function is passed, it is invoked with the current reporter instance.

briefdescription.para: Output operator for nullptr.

detaileddescription.para:
Reference to the current reporter instance.
This operator overload appends the string "nullptr" to the internal output buffer of the reporter, as the expression formatter does.

briefdescription.para: Output operator for std::string_view.

detaileddescription.para:
sv
The string view to output.
Reference to the current reporter instance.
This operator overload appends the contents of the provided std::string_view to the internal output buffer of the reporter.

briefdescription.para: Output operator to display any pointer.

detaileddescription.para: The char pointers are excluded, so that they are output as strings by the const char* overload, as the const char pointers are.

T
The type pointed to, other than char.
v
The pointer value to output.
Reference to the current reporter instance.
The address is formatted by the detail::append_pointer() helper, shared with the detail::expression_formatter, so that the pointers are displayed identically in the expressions and in the messages.

briefdescription.para: Output operator for arithmetic types.

detaileddescription.para:
T
The arithmetic type.
v
The value to output.
Reference to the current reporter instance.
This template operator overload allows the reporter to output values of any arithmetic type (integral or floating-point) in a consistent and readable format. The value is formatted using the detail::append_number() helper, without a type suffix (unlike the detail::expression_formatter operators, which add one).

briefdescription.para: Deleted copy assignment operator to prevent copying.

detaileddescription.para: The reporter owns the output buffer and the output file, which must not be shared.

briefdescription.para: Deleted move assignment operator to prevent moving.

detaileddescription.para: The reporter is owned by the runner, through a pointer, and is never relocated.

briefdescription.para: Reports a passed condition.

detaileddescription.para:
message
The message to display.
expression
The string representation of the expression.
test_case
The test case that owns this check.
Returns
Nothing.
Outputs a pass prefix, followed by either the provided message or, if the message is empty, the evaluated expression string itself. A pass suffix is then appended to complete the output.

briefdescription.para: Reports a test suite skipped by the filter.

detaileddescription.para: Displays an ok <index> - <name> # SKIP filtered line, instead of the suite body and results.

suite
Reference to the skipped test suite.
Returns
Nothing.
Emits an ok <index> - <name> # SKIP filtered line, with the name escaped (see tap_text()), without a test case block, so that the suite keeps its place in the TAP plan of the session. The line is written to the output file when one is open. Unless verbosity is silent, it is also written to stdout; under normal or verbose verbosity, it is preceded by a blank line when add_empty_line_ is set. With quiet verbosity, it is written as the result lines of end_suite(), which the session plan counts.

briefdescription.para: Reports a test case skipped by the filter.

detaileddescription.para: Displays an ok <index> - <name> # SKIP filtered line, indented by its nesting depth.

test_case
Reference to the skipped test case.
Returns
Nothing.
As in begin_test_case(), for a nested test case, the results of the checks already performed by the outer test case, if any, are written first (see commit_outer_results()), so that the output follows the execution order.

An ok <index> - <name> # SKIP filtered line, with the name escaped, indented according to the nesting depth, without a test case block, is then written to the output file and, under normal or verbose verbosity, to stdout, after the headings of the outer test cases, if not displayed yet, and, under verbose verbosity, preceded by a blank line when add_empty_line_ is set.

briefdescription.para: Returns whether the passed checks are written anywhere.

detaileddescription.para: Called by test_case::expect() and test_case::require(), so that a passed check whose line is never written does not format its expression, its messages, or its line. The answer depends only on the verbosity and on the output file, which do not change during the session. A failed check is always formatted.

Parameters
None.
true
The lines of the passed checks reach the console or the output file, at least in some cases.
false
The lines of the passed checks are never written.
The passed checks are written to the output file, when it is open, whatever the verbosity; to the console only with the verbose verbosity level. With the normal verbosity, only the failed checks (with the names of the open test cases) are displayed, so the passed checks are only counted, without formatting them.

briefdescription.para: Writes the results buffered for the outer test case before a nested test case begins.

detaileddescription.para: Keeps the TAP stream in execution order, with the checks of the outer test case before the nested test case, as node-tap does.

Parameters
None.
Returns
Nothing.
The buffered ok/not ok lines of the outer test case are always written to the output file and, with normal or verbose verbosity, to stdout, after the headings of the outer test cases, if not displayed yet, and preceded by an empty line when add_empty_line_ is set. They are displayed even if all the checks passed, since the outer test case, which contains a nested test case, is displayed as a block, whose plan counts them. With quiet verbosity, only the failed checks are displayed, as comments. The buffer is then cleared, so that the nested test case starts with an empty buffer, and the remaining lines of the outer test case are written by its end_test_case().

briefdescription.para: Displays the # Subtest: headings not yet displayed, of the open test cases.

detaileddescription.para: With normal verbosity, a test case is displayed as a single test point, unless it contains a nested test case or a failure; its heading is therefore displayed only when something is displayed under it, outermost first, so that the displayed test points remain the complete content of the block.

include_last
Whether to display the heading of the innermost open test case too; false for the single test point of a passed test case, which has no block.
Returns
Nothing.
Walks open_test_cases_ from the outermost test case and writes, to stdout, the indented "# Subtest: <name>" line of each one whose heading was not displayed yet, with the line breaks in the name replaced by spaces, marking it as displayed. Each heading is preceded by a blank line when add_empty_line_ is set; the flag is then cleared, so that the content of the block follows its heading.

memberdef.argsstring: (const std::string &message, const bool has_expression, const reflection::source_location &location, const test_case &test_case) override
memberdef.name: output_fail_prefix

briefdescription.para: Outputs the prefix for a failing condition.

detaileddescription.para:
message
The message to display.
has_expression
Whether the failure is associated with an expression.
location
The source location of the failure.
test_case
The test case that owns this check.
Returns
Nothing.
This member function outputs the prefix for a failing check result, as a TAP "not ok <n>" line, indented one level deeper than the test case, followed by the message, if provided, escaped (see tap_text()), so that a # does not start a directive and a line break does not end the test point line. It then opens the TAP 14 YAML diagnostics block (---) and, when the failure has an expression, starts a condition: field, so that the expression follows on the same line; the position where the expression begins is kept in condition_begin_, so that output_fail_suffix() can quote it. Without an expression, condition_begin_ is set to std::string::npos. No colours are used.

memberdef.argsstring: (const reflection::source_location &location, check_kind kind, const test_case &test_case) override
memberdef.name: output_fail_suffix

briefdescription.para: Outputs the suffix for a failing condition.

detaileddescription.para:
location
The source location of the failure.
kind
The kind of the check; not used, since a failed requirement is reported like any other failed check.
test_case
The test case that owns this check.
Returns
Nothing.
Completes the TAP 14 YAML diagnostics block of a failing check, by ending the line opened by the prefix (the --- line, or the condition: field), adding the at: field with the file name and the line number, and closing the block (...). As for a pass, the streams are flushed when the test case ends.

The location fields are named fileName: and lineNumber:, as written by node-tap; its reporters (for example the JUnit one, used by the CI systems to annotate the failures) read the file name only from fileName: or file:, not from filename:. There is no columnNumber:, since reflection::source_location does not provide a column.

The expression, which follows condition_begin_ in the buffer, is first replaced by its YAML double-quoted form (see yaml_double_quoted()), so that the operands that start a YAML flow collection or a quoted scalar (for example {1, 2} or 'a'), or contain : or #, do not make the diagnostics block invalid.

A failed requirement is reported like any other failed check, as node-tap does for a failed assertion followed by a throw; no marker is added, since any text after --- or after the condition would make the block, or the value, invalid. That the test case stopped is shown by the plan, which follows this test point; without exceptions, the abort of the test execution is reported by the Bail out! line written by abort_session().

briefdescription.para: Outputs the prefix for a passing condition.

detaileddescription.para:
message
The message to display.
test_case
The test case that owns this check.
Returns
Nothing.
This member function outputs the prefix for a passing check result, as a TAP "ok <n> - " line, where <n> is the test point number of the check, which counts the checks and the nested test cases of the test case, indented one level deeper than the test case, followed by the message, if provided. No colours are used.
The position where the description begins is kept in description_begin_, since, when there is no message, the caller appends the expression after this member function returns.
The prefix/suffix member functions help shorten the code generated by the template member functions.

briefdescription.para: Outputs the suffix for a passing condition.

detaileddescription.para:
test_case
The test case that owns this check.
Returns
Nothing.
The description, either the message or the expression, which follows description_begin_ in the buffer, is replaced by its escaped form (see tap_text()), so that a # does not start a directive and a line break does not end the test point line. The pass output is then completed by appending endl, which adds a line ending to the buffer. The streams are not flushed, since nothing was written to them; the buffer is written, and the streams flushed, when the test case ends.
The prefix/suffix member functions help shorten the code generated by the template member functions.

briefdescription.para: Writes the failed checks of the quiet verbosity, as comments.

detaileddescription.para: The quiet verbosity displays the suites as single test points, so the failed checks cannot be displayed as test points of their own, without altering the plan. They are written as TAP comments, preceded by a comment that names the suite and the open test cases, which keeps the console output a valid TAP document. The failed checks are removed from the buffer by clear_buffer(), not by this function. Nothing is written if there is no failed check.

Parameters
None.
Returns
Nothing.
Writes a comment line with the names of the suite and of the open test cases, separated by " > ", with the line breaks replaced by spaces, then the lines of failures_, each prefixed by the comment prefix. The lines of the failed checks keep their indentation, after the prefix, so that the YAML diagnostics blocks remain readable. The output is not buffered; failures_ is not cleared.

briefdescription.para: Size of the array that receives the elapsed time text.

detaileddescription.para: Large enough for ", time: 4294967295.999 ms", the longest text produced by format_elapsed_time().

briefdescription.para: Number of spaces per nesting level.

detaileddescription.para: Used by the concrete reporters to indent the lines of the nested test cases; four spaces is also the TAP 14 subtest indentation.

briefdescription.para: Size of the array that receives the totals text.

detaileddescription.para: Large enough for the longest text produced by format_session_totals(), which is longer than the texts of the suites and of the test cases: 53 characters, four counts, two fragments of up to 20 characters and a count each (the longest fragment is ", N test cases failed"), and the terminator, with the counts of the largest size_t value (10 digits on 32-bit targets, 20 on 64-bit ones). The fragments are counted at their maximum length, as the compiler does when it checks for truncation.
The array is a local variable of the functions that end the test cases, which run at the deepest point of the stack, so it is not larger than needed on the 32-bit embedded targets.

briefdescription.para: Whether to write an empty line before the next console output.

detaileddescription.para: Set and cleared by the concrete reporters, to separate the groups of console lines, such as the suites and the failed test cases; the output file is not affected.

briefdescription.para: Output accumulation buffer.

detaileddescription.para: Accumulates all reporter output until it is written to the console or the output file via write_console_text() or write_buffer_to_file().

briefdescription.para: Whether the output buffer contains a failed check.

detaileddescription.para: Set by fail() and reset by clear_buffer(). When a nested test case begins, the concrete reporters use it to decide whether the results already buffered for the outer test case are displayed with normal verbosity.

briefdescription.para: ANSI colour codes for output formatting.

detaileddescription.para: Empty strings by default; the human reporter assigns detail::colours_red_green when colours are enabled by runner_options::colour, explicitly or because the console is a terminal.

briefdescription.para: The suite that has begun and not yet ended.

detaileddescription.para: Set by enter_suite(); null outside the suites.

briefdescription.para: Expression formatter for pass and fail reporting.

detaileddescription.para: Used by the checks (test_case::expect(), test_case::require(), and detail::check_result), which are friends, to pre-format expressions at construction time; pass() and fail() then append the formatted text to buffer_. The applications format their own types by defining operator<< for the public expression_formatter alias.

briefdescription.para: The lines of the failed checks, for the quiet verbosity.

detaileddescription.para: With the quiet verbosity, the console displays only the failed checks, while buffer_ may also contain the passed checks, for the output file. Filled by mark_failure() and emptied by clear_buffer(); not used with the other verbosity levels.

briefdescription.para: Whether the output file could not be opened.

detaileddescription.para: Set by the constructor, and returned by has_output_file_error(). Kept next to the other flags, so that the class does not end with padding, which the derived classes would report.

briefdescription.para: The test cases that have begun and not yet ended, outermost first.

detaileddescription.para: The last element is the test case that owns the buffered results.

briefdescription.para: Optional output file, receiving a copy of the test report.

detaileddescription.para: When non-null, the report is written to this file in addition to the console, without colour sequences. The file receives the full report, regardless of the verbosity. The file is opened by the constructor and closed by the destructor.

briefdescription.para: Path of the optional output file.

detaileddescription.para: Copied by the constructor from the session options. Used to name the file in the confirmation message displayed when the file is closed (not displayed with the silent verbosity).

briefdescription.para: Whether the heading of the current suite was displayed on the console.

detaileddescription.para: Set by enter_suite(); with the quiet verbosity, which does not display the headings, the heading is displayed when the first failure of the suite is.

briefdescription.para: The verbosity level for test reporting.

detaileddescription.para: A copy of the level kept by the runner, set by the constructor from the same session options and not changed afterwards. The public accessor is runner::verbosity_level().

briefdescription.para: Clears the output buffer.

detaileddescription.para: Also resets buffer_has_failures_, so that the flag always describes the current content of the buffer.

Parameters
None.
Returns
Nothing.
Empties buffer_ and failures_, keeping their capacity, and resets buffer_has_failures_.

briefdescription.para: Writes the results of the outer test case, if any, before a nested test case begins or is skipped.

detaileddescription.para: Called by begin_test_case() and skip_test_case() of the concrete reporters, so that the output follows the execution order.

Parameters
None.
Returns
Nothing.
For a nested test case, the outer test case may have performed checks before it; their results are written first, by commit_buffer(). For a top-level test case, the buffer is expected to be empty, since the checks are performed only by the test cases, and each one writes its results when it ends; should it not be, its content is written in the same way, rather than lost or attributed to the next test case, and the run continues.

briefdescription.para: Returns the buffered lines that the console displays when a test case or a suite ends, or when its results are committed.

detaileddescription.para: With the verbose verbosity, all the buffered lines; with the normal verbosity, all the buffered lines of a failed test case or suite, otherwise none; with the quiet verbosity, only the lines of the failed checks; with the silent verbosity, none.

failed
Whether the test case or the suite failed, or, when committing the results of an outer test case, whether the buffer contains a failed check.
A view of buffer_ or of failures_, valid until they are modified.
The quiet verbosity displays the failed checks, and the buffer may also contain the passed checks, for the output file; the lines of the failed checks are therefore kept separately, in failures_.

briefdescription.para: Notes the suite that begins, for the headings displayed later.

detaileddescription.para: Called by begin_suite() of the concrete reporters, with the information whether the heading of the suite was displayed.

suite
The suite that begins.
displayed
Whether the heading was written to the console.
Returns
Nothing.
Records the suite and whether its heading was displayed; the quiet verbosity displays it later, if the suite has a failure.

briefdescription.para: Records that the lines appended to the buffer from a given position are a failure.

detaileddescription.para: Sets buffer_has_failures_ and, with the quiet verbosity, which displays only the failures, copies the lines to failures_.

begin
The position in buffer_ where the lines of the failure begin.
Returns
Nothing.
Only the quiet verbosity needs the copy, since the other levels display the buffer as a whole, or nothing.

briefdescription.para: Tells where a kind of record is written.

detaileddescription.para: The headings of the test cases that contain a failure are also displayed with the normal verbosity (see console_lines()), but the passed checks are not; they are only counted, without being formatted (see writes_passed_checks()). The concrete reporters adapt the quiet and normal levels to their format.

kind
The kind of record.
The destinations of the record.
The file receives all the records, when it is open, so that its content does not depend on the verbosity (a file of a silent run is as complete as that of a verbose one). The console follows the verbosity levels, as documented in the declaration.

briefdescription.para: Writes the current buffered content to the output file.

detaileddescription.para: The buffer is written without appending a line ending, and is not cleared. ANSI colour sequences are removed, so the file receives plain text even when the console output is coloured. If no output file is open, the call has no effect.

Parameters
None.
Returns
Nothing.
Writes the contents of buffer_ to output_file_ without appending a newline. If output_file_ is null, the call is a no-op.
The buffer may contain ANSI colour sequences, added when the console is a terminal, which must not reach the file; they are removed by write_without_colours().

briefdescription.para: Writes formatted text to the console.

detaileddescription.para: All reporter console output is routed through this function, so that it reaches the standard output stream via a single path, shared with the output of the user printf() calls. Using one stream-based path keeps the reporter and user output in the same buffer, preserving their relative order.

format
A printf()-style format string.
...
The arguments referred to by the format string.
Returns
Nothing.
The arguments are forwarded to vfprintf() on stdout. The stream is explicit, so the compiler does not rewrite the call into puts() or putchar(), and all console output shares the same FILE-based path.

briefdescription.para: Writes a text to the console, unchanged.

detaileddescription.para: The text is written with its size, not as a C string, so that a zero character in a message does not end the output. No line ending is appended.

text
The text to write.
Returns
Nothing.
The text is written with its size, not as a C string, so that a zero character in a message does not end the output.

briefdescription.para: Writes formatted text to the output file.

detaileddescription.para: If no output file is open, the call has no effect, so callers do not need to check output_file_ themselves.

format
A printf()-style format string.
...
The arguments referred to by the format string.
Returns
Nothing.
The arguments are forwarded to vfprintf() on output_file_. If output_file_ is null, the arguments are ignored.

briefdescription.para: Writes the informational (non-result) lines to the console and to the output file.

detaileddescription.para:
arguments
The command line of the session, listed when not empty; passed by begin_session() from the runner options, so that the reporter does not keep a copy.
Returns
Nothing.
Constructs and emits two informational lines, each prefixed by comment_prefix(): the first lists the program name (without the path) and any command-line arguments; the second identifies the compiler (Clang, GCC, or MSVC) together with the version string, floating-point availability on bare-metal targets, exception support, and any active debug or trace macros. Both lines are written to the output file when one is open, and to stdout when the verbosity is normal or verbose (see route()), except when both MICRO_OS_PLUS_STARTUP_ENABLED and MICRO_OS_PLUS_DIAG_TRACE_ENABLED are defined, since the startup code already displays this information.

briefdescription.para: Writes formatted lines to the output file and, when requested, to the console.

detaileddescription.para: The text is formatted once, and the same text is written to the output file, if open, and, when to_console is true, to stdout. As in write_buffer_to_file(), the ANSI colour sequences are removed from the file copy, so a console line with colours and its plain file line are written by one call. The format normally ends with a line ending; any empty line or buffered output that precedes the console line is written by the caller, before this call.

to_console
Whether to write the text to stdout as well.
format
A printf()-style format string.
...
The arguments referred to by the format string.
Returns
Nothing.
The text is formatted with vsnprintf() into a local array, which holds the usual lines without an allocation; a longer text, for example with a long test name, is formatted again, from a copy of the arguments, into a string of the exact length. The array is kept small, since the lines that end the nested test cases are written at the deepest point of the stack. The text is then written with its length to the output file, without the colour sequences (see write_without_colours()), and, when requested, to stdout, unchanged. When there is nowhere to write, or the formatting fails, nothing is written.

briefdescription.para: Formats the elapsed time of a suite or of the session.

detaileddescription.para: The text is appended to the summary lines by the concrete reporters, in the form ", time: 1.234 ms"; it is empty when the stopwatch has no elapsed time, so that the summary lines remain identical on the platforms without a clock.
The array has a fixed size, known at compile time, so that the compiler can verify that the text is never truncated.

stopwatch
The stopwatch of the suite or of the runner.
message
The character array that receives the null-terminated text.
Returns
Nothing.
The elapsed time, in microseconds, is displayed in milliseconds, with three decimals. When it is zero, either because the stopwatch has no readings or because the interval was shorter than a microsecond, the text is empty.

briefdescription.para: Formats the totals of the test session.

detaileddescription.para: The text is the part of the session summary line common to the concrete reporters, in the form "7 checks passed, 1 failed, in 3 test cases, 2 test suites"; the numbers of test cases and of suites skipped by the filter follow the respective counts, as ", 1 skipped", only when not zero. The label (Total: or total:), the markers, and the elapsed time are added by the callers.

runner
The runner of the test session.
message
The character array that receives the null-terminated text.
Returns
Nothing.
The suites are counted by runner::total_suites_count(), which includes the suites skipped by the filter, counted separately by runner::skipped_suites_count().

briefdescription.para: Formats the totals of a suite.

detaileddescription.para: The text is the part of the suite result line common to the concrete reporters: "7 checks in 3 test cases" for a passed suite, and "6 checks passed, 1 failed, in 3 test cases" for a failed one; the number of test cases skipped by the filter follows, as ", 1 skipped", only when not zero. The status, the enclosing markers, and the elapsed time are added by the callers.

suite
The suite that ended.
message
The character array that receives the null-terminated text.
Returns
Nothing.
A passed suite has no failed checks, so only the number of checks is shown.

briefdescription.para: Formats the totals of a test case.

detaileddescription.para: The text is the part of the test case result line common to the concrete reporters: "7 checks" for a passed test case, and "6 checks passed, 1 failed" for a failed one, followed by the number of failed nested test cases, as ", 1 test case failed", only when not zero, since a test case may fail because of a nested one alone. The status and the enclosing markers are added by the callers.

test_case
The test case that ended.
message
The character array that receives the null-terminated text.
Returns
Nothing.
A passed test case has no failed checks and no failed nested test cases, so only the number of checks is shown.

briefdescription.para: TAP (Test Anything Protocol) implementation of reporter.

detaileddescription.para: reporter_tap provides a concrete implementation of the reporter abstract interface that formats test results according to the Test Anything Protocol (TAP). It accumulates output in an internal string buffer and writes it to the standard output stream.

The reporter is created by the runner, as selected by the --reporter command-line option, or by runner_options::selected_reporter; it is the default. A different output format requires a new class derived from reporter, and an extension of the runner to create it.
All members are defined within the micro_os_plus::micro_test_plus::detail namespace, since the reporters are internal to the framework.
